concept.name: Time under water
concept.definition: The time an investment's equity spends below its high-water mark — the duration view of drawdown, visualized by the underwater curve and summarized by longest or average episode length.
concept.intuition: It measures how long investors are 'drowning' relative to their peak, capturing the opportunity cost and psychological burden that depth-only statistics miss.
concept.mechanics: Compute the running drawdown series; each contiguous stretch of nonzero drawdown is one time-under-water episode with a start (last peak), a depth path, and an end (recovery to the peak). Reported statistics include longest episode, current episode, and average episode length.
concept.formula: TUW over (0,T) = integral_0^T 1{D(t) > 0} dt, where D(t) is the drawdown at time t and 1{} the indicator function.
concept.failure_modes: Like all drawdown-path statistics it is sample- and frequency-dependent, and unrecovered drawdowns at the sample end censor the measurement. Within an episode it ignores magnitude unless paired with depth statistics.
concept.misconceptions: Time under water is not the same as losing money continuously: equity can rise during most of an episode while still sitting below the old high-water mark.
concept.example: A strategy that made its last equity high ten months ago and is still 5% below it has a current time under water of ten months.
